headline: Adjusted profit grows on digital push, GAAP EPS slides

drivers.explanation: Growth led by Payments Infrastructure (+11%, CoreCard contribution plus acquiring and Ren infrastructure sales) and epay (+5%), partly offset by Cross-Border Payments revenue falling 4%.

Consolidated operating income fell as Cross-Border Payments operating income dropped 34% on weaker U.S. outbound remittance volumes tied to immigration-policy changes and a non-repeating Pakistan fee rebate.
Decline driven by the same Cross-Border Payments weakness (segment Adjusted EBITDA -31%), partly offset by growth in Payments Infrastructure (+7%) and epay (+5%).
Fell on lower operating income plus income tax expense rising to $46.7M from $33.6M, partly offset by lower interest expense after quarter-end debt refinancing.
Rose despite the GAAP decline because non-GAAP addbacks shrank (FX loss fell to $0.2M from $5.7M) and the adjusted-EPS share count fell from the convertible-note dilution add-back.
Tracks the Cross-Border Payments operating-income decline and higher income tax expense, only partly offset by lower net interest expense.
Rose after the company repaid roughly $700 million of maturing senior notes using revolving-credit-facility borrowings, shifting debt from short-term to long-term.

CEO framed results as resilient: digital accelerators (CoreCard, merchant acquiring, Dandelion) grew 31% y/y to roughly 26% of revenue, even as GAAP profit fell on Cross-Border Payments remittance headwinds.

summary_short: Revenue rose 3.2% y/y to $1,108.4 million as digital-accelerator revenue grew 31% y/y to roughly 26% of sales, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 24.7% to $1.71 while adjusted diluted EPS rose 10.2% to $2.82.
summary_long: Payments Infrastructure grew constant-currency revenue 10%, aided by acquiring, Ren infrastructure sales and the CoreCard acquisition, while epay grew 4% on higher-value digital content despite an 11% transaction-count drop from low-value India volumes. Cross-Border Payments revenue fell 5% in constant currency as U.S. immigration-policy pressure cut outbound remittance volumes and a favorable Pakistan fee rebate did not repeat, dragging segment operating income down 35%; digital money-transfer transactions still rose 33%. GAAP operating income fell 13.6% on the CBP weakness and higher tax expense, while adjusted EPS rose 10.2% on non-GAAP addbacks. The company repurchased $50 million of stock, repaid roughly $700 million of maturing notes with revolver borrowings, and reiterated FY2026 adjusted EPS growth guidance of 10%-15%.
